newsitem.title: USA: New York man admits to role in IBM check scheme.
newsitem.headline: New York man admits to role in IBM check scheme.

text.p: A New York man admitted Tuesday to his role in a scheme to cash six stolen IBM checks totalling $330,000, the U.S. Attorney in New Jersey said.

Vito Pietanza, 47, of Brooklyn, N.Y., faces a miximum of five years in federal prison, a $250,000 fine and repayment of the monies when he is sentenced by U.S. District Judge William H. Walls, according to Assistant U.S. Attorney Noel L. Hillman.
Other participants in the scheme were an unidentified New Jersey lawyer and two others.
The checks were mailed in 1992 from International Business Machines Corp. in San Jose, Calif., to a freight-forwarding firm, Schenkers International, in Freeport, N.Y.
Six checks issued to Schenkers from IBM totalled $333,415.30 but never arrived at Schenkers' office.
Last year, Anthony Costa, a Staten Island, N.Y., resident, pleaded guilty in Newark Federal Court to interstate transportation of stolen property in the case.
Costa told an unidentified individual that the checks belonged to two owners of Schenkers who wanted to convert the proceeds to their personal use.
Pietanza admitted that he cashed three checks totalling $17,000 that were made out to him, then returned the proceeds to Costa and one unidentified individual.
U.S. Attorney Faith S. Hochberg said the FBI and the Criminal Investigation Division of the Internal Revenue Service assisted in developing the case against Pietanza.
